text: Hi guys. So if you take a look at this
picture, you would feel that this is
Dubai, not Gurudong. But the moment you
walk out of your society's gated
complex, you will start seeing everyday
problems, right? From potholes to dogs
running after you to bite you and poor
drainage system, etc., etc. But this
does not stop Guram from blatantly
copying whatever is happening in the
Dubai real estate market. And this makes
no sense. For example, in Gurong, what
is happening at a builder level is that
they have started giving contracts to
agents to pump up the property. An agent
will end up locking like 10, 15 houses.
The builder will come out with full
paged ads that you know what our project
get sold off and that's that. Something
similar happens in Dubai but the market
is very regulated. For example, in order
to become a broker in Dubai, you need a
license. It is called as RA license. You
can't just simply go and start selling
properties. But no such license is
required in Guruda. Second key point is
around flexible payment plans. Again
many developers in Dubai give like 1%
payment plan etc etc. But again the
regulations in Dubai are that a builder
has to maintain and put money into an
escrow account. In India too we have
something called as RAA registered
projects and the builder is supposed to
put money into those accounts but this
is many a times not followed and RARA is
not foolproof. Third and finally, what
we miss about the Dubai versus Guruda
real estate market is that in Dubai
there are proper laws to protect the
tenant, right, and protect the buyers.
In fact, that just does not apply only
to Guruda. It applies anywhere in India
because our judiciary is kind of weak.
So, in case you're looking to buy a
property, Indian real estate is great.
I'm not doing any fear-mongering. All
I'm simply trying to tell you is that
you need to understand these points and
do your proper due diligence before
buying.
